findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9–11 unconditionally accesses [0]['id'] on the category query result, crashing the migration and blocking upgrades when embed_category is unset or matches no existing category.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 preserves URL schemes when migrating existing hosts, causing values such as https://example.com to fail the new hostname-only lookup and breaking embedding.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting valid domains such as example.museum and preventing administrators from adding or editing them.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15–18 allows saved hosts containing ports, but lookup uses uri.host without the port, so entries such as example.com:8080 never match requests.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting valid domains such as example.museum and preventing administrators from adding or editing them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Valid TLDs like .museum (6 chars), .technology (10 chars), and many new gTLDs exceed 5 characters. This is a real bug that would prevent administrators from adding hosts with longer TLDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15–18 allows saved hosts containing ports, but lookup uses uri.host without the port, so entries such as example.com:8080 never match requests.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model: the validation regex allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation strips the protocol and path but NOT the port. So a host like 'example.com:8080' could be saved. In record_for_host(), it uses `uri = URI(host)` then `host = uri.host`. URI parsing extracts just the hostname without port (uri.host returns 'example.com' not 'example.com:8080'). The lookup does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` comparing against the stored value. If 'example.com:8080' is stored but the lookup uses 'example.com', they won't match. This is a real bug - hosts with ports in the database won't be found during lookups.
